key_insight: This review traces how materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to multimodal LLMs and agentic systems supporting materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Automated literature extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs and support research assistants and autonomous laboratory workflows.
method: Reviews rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, LLM and agentic extraction approaches.
Examines extraction from text, tables and figures.
Assesses generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs and pipeline design.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a critical assessment of datasets, accuracy and costs, but reports no quantitative results and highlights scarce reliable benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linking of structure, properties, processing and performance remains an open challenge.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
